facts.claim: Top-quartile consumer apps hold 25% to 40% at day 30 and their curves flatten between day 60 and day 90
facts.excerpt: Top-quartile consumer apps see Day 30 retention of 25 to 40 percent and flatten by Day 60 to 90.

facts.claim: The mobile day-30 average runs 7% to 8%, with strong products above 15%
facts.source_title: The complete guide to measuring user retention
facts.excerpt: Mobile benchmark for Day 30 is 7-8% average, 15%+ for strong products.

facts.claim: SaaS subscription products often reach 40% to 50% day-30 retention, several times the mobile average
facts.source_title: The complete guide to measuring user retention
facts.excerpt: SaaS subscription products often hit 40-50% Day 30 retention.

facts.claim: Social apps retain a median 40% at day 1, 18% at day 7 and 12% at day 30, with strong performers at 50-60%, 25-30% and 15-20%
facts.source_title: App Retention Benchmarks: How Your App Stacks Up by Industry
facts.excerpt: Social apps: strong performers 50-60% Day-1, 25-30% Day-7, 15-20% Day-30; medians 40%, 18% and 12%.

facts.claim: E-commerce apps retain a median 18% at day 1, 5% at day 7 and 2% at day 30, with strong performers at 25-30%, 8-12% and 3-6%
facts.source_title: App Retention Benchmarks: How Your App Stacks Up by Industry
facts.excerpt: Ecommerce apps: strong performers 25-30% Day-1, 8-12% Day-7, 3-6% Day-30; medians 18%, 5% and 2%.

facts.claim: Gaming apps retain a median 32% at day 1, 8% at day 7 and 3% at day 30, with strong performers at 40-50%, 12-18% and 5-8%
facts.source_title: App Retention Benchmarks: How Your App Stacks Up by Industry
facts.excerpt: Gaming apps: strong performers 40-50% Day-1, 12-18% Day-7, 5-8% Day-30; medians 32%, 8% and 3%.

facts.claim: India's app market earned 3.8 billion dollars in 2024, up 15.1% on the year before
facts.excerpt: The Indian app market earned $3.8 billion revenue in 2024, a 15.1% increase on the year prior.

gaps: No published India day-1 to day-30 retention curve by app category. Regional download-to-paid conversion exists; the retention curve does not.
contradictions: The mobile day-30 retention average is published incompatibly across sources: countly.com gives 7% to 8% with strong products above 15%, while uxcam.com puts the cross-industry figure at 4% and userpilot.com at 5.7% across 31 categories. The sources differ on which apps enter the denominator and on whether the figure is a mean or a median, and none publishes enough method to reconcile them. This page uses the countly band and names the spread rather than averaging the three.
